title: Access points are placed in Mapping
body_markdown:
### New
- **Wi-Fi access points on the Atlas.** With UniFi Utopia, each access point is a Home Assistant device, and Mapping places it like any other device: it has its own symbol and the "Wi-Fi" filter. The Wi-Fi coverage screen draws each one where it is placed (until then dashed, where the devices that hear it best suggest), and "Place in Mapping" opens Mapping with that access point selected.

### Changed
- **Wi-Fi coverage no longer drags access points.** One place to put them: Mapping.
- **The note under far-access-point findings** says devices differ in their transmitters and antennas, not only antennas.

title: A fairer accuracy score; PDF floor plans
body_markdown:
### New
- **PDF floor plans in Mapping → Upload.** Pick a PDF the way you pick a picture. PadSpan draws the page in your browser, and the upload goes on as for any image, with the same crop, size and scale steps. When a PDF has several pages, you choose the one with the plan. Drawn plans (an architect's or a builder's export) stay sharp because the page is drawn, not photographed. Black-and-white scans from an office scanner or a permit office work too. A password-protected or broken PDF says so. Nothing extra loads unless you pick a PDF.

### Fixed
- **Calibration's "How accurate it is now" counts only what it can test.** Four changes to how the score is worked out:
  - A room calibrated at one spot only is listed as not counted. It used to count as wrong, because the test holds out the spot and its neighbours and nothing of that room was left.
  - A spot's true room is the room drawn where it stands, not a label that disagrees with it. How many disagree is shown.
  - Spots heard by a single receiver are left out, as live tracking leaves them out.
  - In a big calibration, each room is tested in proportion to its spots.
  On a real house the score went from 4 % to 29 % rooms right for fingerprints, and from 12 % to 28 % for spatial, on the same data.
  Nothing about how positions are worked out changed. If you turned on "pick the better method", the comparison it makes now uses this fairer score. The opt-in report counts how many rooms couldn't be tested (a number, never a name).

title: Wi-Fi coverage says what to fix
body_markdown:
### New
- **Wi-Fi coverage (test): what to fix, first.** Above the map, UniFi Utopia's findings, most urgent first, each with what to do: placed devices that keep dropping off Wi-Fi, that sit on a far access point while a neighbour a few metres away hears another one much better, that are very weak, PadSpan receivers on weak Wi-Fi (their reports arrive late or not at all), rooms where a phone spends time on weak Wi-Fi, and before and after for a device that moved to another access point. A click shows the finding on the plan.
- **Access points on the plan.** Each access point is drawn where you put it, or (dashed) where the devices that hear it best suggest. An administrator drags one to where it really is, or sets its floor under "Where the access points are".

### Changed
- **UniFi Blocker is now UniFi Utopia.** The Wi-Fi coverage tab asks UniFi Utopia (`unifi_utopia/...`) and names it.

title: Small rooms beside bigger ones
body_markdown:
### Fixed
- **A small room along the wall of a bigger one shows sooner.** With your house drawn, a device counts for the next room only once its position is 0.75 m past the wall. A small room such as a bathroom along a bedroom wall is often only 2 m deep, and the position wanders a metre or two, so a stay there was sometimes never shown. Such a room now needs a quarter of its depth (0.5 m for 2 m). Rooms 3 m deep or more, and hallways, keep 0.75 m, so a device standing just inside a doorway does not flicker.

title: Open screens, announcements, links to a room or a person, and a presence sensor per sub-zone
body_markdown:
### New
- **Open screens (off until you turn it on).** Settings → Atlas → 📣 Open screens lists every PadSpan page open right now (wall tablets, TVs, desktops): its name, what it shows, its device, and whether it runs an older PadSpan. You can reload one screen or all of them from there, and rename one ("Kitchen tablet"). Off, PadSpan keeps no list.
- **Announcements on your screens.** The new action `padspan_ha.announce` puts a message big over the open PadSpan screens for a few seconds, with a chime. It can read the message aloud and can go to only the screens you name. Use it for the doorbell, the washing machine or dinner. `padspan_ha.reload_screens` reloads them from an automation. Both need Open screens switched on.
- **Links to a room or a person.** `/padspan-ha?room=Kitchen` opens that room's card, and `/padspan-ha?follow=Alex` opens Follow on that tag. Both work from a notification on your phone.
- **A presence sensor for a sub-zone.** In Mapping → Edit → Sub-zones, a bed, couch or desk can have its own presence sensor, such as an mmWave zone like an Aqara FP2's "Sofa". While that sensor is on, a tagged person in that room counts as in the sub-zone even before their position gets there. Bluetooth says who, the sensor says when. It only ever adds, and how positions and rooms are worked out doesn't change. Sub-zones themselves stay off until you turn them on.

title: Wi-Fi coverage keeps itself up to date
body_markdown:
### Fixed
- **Wi-Fi coverage (test) updates by itself.** It loaded its readings once and then stayed as it was until a button was pressed; it now asks UniFi Blocker again each minute while it is open, and waits while a picker is open.
- **Both bands have their button from the start.** 2.4 and 5 GHz are always there, so 5 GHz no longer seems to be missing before the first phone reading; the screen opens on a floor that has readings in the band it shows.
- **The access point picker is as wide as its names**, not the whole screen.

title: The German guides name the German panel's buttons; The German manual names the German panel's labels; Wi-Fi coverage from UniFi Blocker (a test)
body_markdown:
### New
- **Wi-Fi coverage, a test.** With UniFi Blocker's Wi-Fi survey installed, a new tab under Diagnose shows how strongly your access points hear each part of the house, measured in everyday use: phones while they sit still for a minute, and smart devices where PadSpan has them placed. It is drawn on PadSpan's own floor model in the radio map's colours, one map per band, with each room's typical reading. Without UniFi Blocker the tab does not appear and nothing changes.

### Changed
- **The German website guides name PadSpan's buttons and menus as the German panel shows them**, now that most of the panel is German: "Einstellungen → Ortung → Leistung → Speichersparmodus" where they said "Settings → Tracking → Performance → Low-memory mode", "Wer ist wo", "Eine Karte daraus machen", "Kalibrierung → Modell" and so on, in all fifteen guides. Where a screen is still English (the Atlas, Live Aboard, the Wall screens card, the Guests screen, the Claude room helper and the robot vacuum import), a guide keeps its English names and says so. The note that PadSpan's menus are in English is gone from the guides and from the German home page.

### Fixed
- **Der deutsche Handbuchtext nennt die Bezeichnungen, die das Panel jetzt auf Deutsch zeigt**: PadSpan-Lizenz, iPhone-Einrichtungsweg, MAC-Wechsel überbrücken, Forensik, Deine KI und die beiden Atlas-Schalter. (The German manual uses the panel's German names for these settings.)

title: The manual on the website, in English and German, and it says what the panel says; Walk a room on by default; a notification for leak, smoke, gas and CO alarms; area renames follow; Manage, Training and Settings in German, French and Dutch; Steadier rooms; Why rooms jump: the guide says how the vote works with 40 seconds
body_markdown:
### New
- **The PadSpan HA Manual is on the website**, at padspan.traks.ca/manual/: the contents page and a page for each of its 27 chapters and four appendices, with links between chapters and to each section. The pages are made from the manual in the repository every time it changes, so the website says what the manual says. The guides page and the home page link it, and PadSpan's entry in Home Assistant now points its documentation link there.
- **The manual in German**, at padspan.traks.ca/manual/de/: every chapter and appendix, in the panel's German words, and in English where a screen is still English. The reference tables made from the code (entities, settings, the menu, every screen and tab, the websocket commands) stay in English inside the German chapters, so they always match the code.
- **Renaming an area in Home Assistant renames its PadSpan room.** Before, the room stayed under the old name and showed as "PadSpan only, not a Home Assistant area". Now its outline, details, neighbours, receivers, floor-plan bounds, calibration points, Follow alerts that watch it, what PadSpan learned about it and the room–tag map all take the new name, after an automatic backup ("Before renaming room …"), with one line in Home Assistant's log. Past records (movement history, lost-and-found, recordings) keep the old name, and so do guest stays, sub-zone labels, the Live Aboard director's room list and the ESPresense room map. If PadSpan already has a room with the new name, nothing is renamed. A rename made while PadSpan isn't running is not seen.
- **A leak, smoke, gas or CO alarm sends a notification.** When one latches, PadSpan sends one notification ("PadSpan: Leak alarm", with the sensor, its room and the time), and one when it clears: reset in the Atlas, or the 2 days over. Nothing more while it stays latched, however often the sensor goes off again. It goes to the phones and email addresses your Follow alerts send to; with none set, to the first notify service Home Assistant has (a mail one first), as a Follow alert with no target does; with no notify service at all, nothing is sent. On by default: Settings → Atlas → Atlas — Mapped Light Control → "Notify when a leak, smoke, gas or CO alarm goes off".
- **Manage speaks German, French and Dutch.** When your Home Assistant profile is set to one of them, every Manage tab is in your language: Data (the danger zone, orphan room shapes, BLE device names, phantom entries, Home Assistant entities, areas and maps, Backup & Restore, integration controls), HA Entities (the entity reference and library, publishing controls, the live inventory, MQTT, Tasmota and ESPresense), Beacon Characteristics, History, Events and the email alerts, Logs and Factory Reset. Entity IDs, attribute names and the YAML examples stay as Home Assistant reads them, and Factory Reset still asks you to type FACTORY RESET.
- **Training speaks German, French and Dutch too:** the hub, every walkthrough with its animated diagrams, the Quick Start and the Full Manual. The note that some of Training was still in English is gone.
- **All of Settings speaks German, French and Dutch.** When your Home Assistant profile is set to one of them, Features (the PadSpan licence card, its homes list, the tiers tour, the experimental features and Forensics), AI (your AI Task, its usage line and the map-building research switches), Atlas (outdoor weather, Live Aboard's settings, what it flies to, scenes and the Atlas as Overview) and UI Structure are in your language.
- Live Aboard's own buttons and menus are still in English, so Settings names them in English too ("Views ▾ → Show people", "Line up plans").
- The Atlas and the 3D view are still in English; they come next.

### Changed
- **The room-flapping guide describes the new default.** With Room Change Delay at 40 seconds, PadSpan keeps the last eight checks and a new room must win five (all eight for 30 seconds after a move). English and German.
- **Walk a room is on by default, and Setup offers it first.** Setup's Calibrate step now starts with the 90-second walk per room, with "Point by point" beside it for Guided calibration. A new install has it on. An install from before is switched on once by this update, unless a walk was saved there: then it was on and someone turned it off, and it stays off. Turn it off or on again in Settings → Tracking → Positioning and calibration → Walk a Room (Calibration).
- **Two settings nothing used are no longer taken.** `auto_offset_mode` and `signal_loss_linger_s` were accepted by the settings command and read by nothing; the command now refuses them. A value already saved stays in the settings file untouched. `occupancy_multiplier` (0.5 to 10) and `occupancy_dwell_min` (0 to 60 minutes) were handled but refused by the command's checks; they are now taken.
- **The manual, checked against the code and against Home Assistant's own pages.** Chapter 21's list of what always needs an administrator is now the whole list (it left out the AI features, recordings, Forensics, the licence, imports, the layout's bigger steps, sub-zones, WLED settings and more). Chapters 15 and 25 say power teams are in the free edition. Chapter 3 says how to get betas from the Marketplace (its Pre-release switch), that updates are in Settings → Updates on 2026.11, and how to uninstall from the Marketplace. Appendix D's command table has plain lines where a handler's own description was a developer's note or missing.
- **Room Change Delay is now 40 seconds unless you set it.** It was 20 seconds. On two recordings of a real house, 40 seconds cut room changes by about a third and the back-and-forth between two neighbouring rooms by about half, and a device lying still was put in the wrong room about a third less often. The cost: when you really move to another room, PadSpan usually shows it about 10 seconds later (on the recording, the carried phone's slowest move came 50 seconds later). If you saved a delay yourself in Settings → Tracking → Rooms and timing, 20 seconds included, PadSpan keeps yours.

### Fixed
- **The manual names what the panel shows.** Its translators found places where the English disagreed with the panel, and each is now fixed in English and German, here and on padspan.traks.ca/manual/. Troubleshooting names Health's ROOMS MIXED UP and FLOOR PLAN cards, the IRK Manager's Test only button and a receiver's Silent … min. The update check is switched off in Settings → Tracking → Privacy, updates and feedback → Update Check. Whole house presets is spelled as the Atlas spells it. A busy house's full update is about 2.2 MB a screen in both the wall-screen and the performance chapters. The AI chapter's only COMING SOON row is Ask your voice assistant where someone is. The accuracy benchmark says that Record asks for the minutes first (1 to 60, 5 unless you change it), and says plainly how live smoothing differs from the per-reading score. Chapter 1 links the manual's own Pro chapter. The German chapters also give the robot vacuum switch its German labels and Room Change Delay's new 40-second default.
- **Home Assistant's "Download diagnostics" hides the tags' addresses.** PadSpan's diagnostics file listed the room–tag map with each tag's key, and a key can be a device's Bluetooth address. Each key is now shown as REDACTED; the rooms and how many tags each has are kept.
- Factory Reset's final warning showed "\n" as text instead of starting new lines.

title: A Zigbee device in ZHA and Zigbee2MQTT counts once
body_markdown:
### New
- **The same Zigbee device in Home Assistant twice is used once.** A device paired through Zigbee2MQTT and still in ZHA (or deCONZ) has the same Zigbee address in both; PadSpan now treats the two as one unit and uses the Zigbee2MQTT one. The other copy is left out of the Atlas, the light index, the room counts, Traceback's replay, Live Aboard's room lists and every list where you pick a device (Settings → Atlas's rain sensor and weather lists, door and lock links, door openers, power teams, Evening lights, Live Aboard's Follows and "This is a device…"), with a quiet "1 duplicate hidden (same unit on Zigbee2MQTT)" where a list is shown. Vacation Mode switches only the Zigbee2MQTT one. The coordinator sticks are never counted as duplicates.
- **A copy you already picked or placed says so.** It stays where it is, with a line naming the Zigbee2MQTT one and a button, Use the Zigbee2MQTT one. Pressed, everything PadSpan keeps for the copy moves to the Zigbee2MQTT one: its place on the map with its looks, label and height, its wall link and invert, its shape and type, hidden from the map, the settings that name it, its power teams, Vacation Mode's lights and Live Aboard's links. Nothing changes until you press it.
- **Told when it happens.** The first time this version runs, one Home Assistant notification lists the devices already in two integrations; after that, a new copy is named as it appears, once for each pair. PadSpan notices it from Home Assistant's own device list (no polling) and never changes Home Assistant itself.

title: Beacon Tune pins a beacon only when you say so; Power teams: brightness and colour apart, bedtime, a night light, and more for the wake-up; It no longer rains on the Atlas because of a rain sensor stuck on wet
body_markdown:
### New
- **Dimming keeps the colour on the day.** A brightness set by hand (at the wall dimmer, on the card or at a bulb) stops the day leading the brightness only; the colour goes on following the day. A colour set by hand does the same the other way round. The card says which is set by hand.
- **Back to the day by itself.** Each team can hand a change by hand back to the day after a time you choose (30 minutes to 8 hours), as well as at the next turn-on. A wake-up's light goes back to the day a set time after its full light (an hour unless you change it).
- **Bedtime.** On the days and at the time you choose, a team that is on fades to Sleep, warmer as it dims, then turns off or stays in Sleep. The card also has **Sleep in 30 min** for tonight only.
- **Night light.** Between the hours you choose, a team switched on (at the wall, with a tap, or by an automation) comes on dim and warm instead of at the day's light. A brightness asked for is still given.
- **Wake-up:** skip the next morning with one press, a different time on Saturday and Sunday, and it now wakes a room left on in Sleep, from there.
- **The day's curve:** an earliest and latest sunrise and sunset, so a summer dawn at five does not light a bedroom before half past six.

### Fixed
- **Placing a beacon no longer pins it.** Calibration → Beacon Tune pinned every beacon you placed or dragged there, unless PadSpan knew it moved. A pinned beacon is always shown in its pinned room, and auto-calibration adds points at its spot, so a car key, a tag or a car could end up pinned without anyone deciding it. Now a beacon is pinned only when you tick **Pin here: it never moves** on its row in the Placed Beacons list. Beacons already pinned stay pinned and still move when you drag them; to unpin one, delete it from Beacon Tune.
- **A rain sensor stuck on wet no longer makes it rain.** A rain sensor can stay wet long after the rain has stopped, dirty or with water caught on it, while still reporting as normal. If an on/off rain sensor has said wet for more than 3 hours and your weather entity says it isn't raining or snowing, PadSpan now ignores it until it dries. A shower your forecast missed still shows for its first 3 hours, and once the weather entity says it's raining the sensor is believed again. PadSpan counts the hours itself and keeps them across Home Assistant restarts, because a Zigbee2MQTT sensor looks freshly changed after every restart. A rain gauge, a rain-rate sensor, or an on/off sensor a helper makes from one works as before.
- **Settings tells you.** Under the rain sensor it now says "The rain sensor has said wet for over 3 hours while the forecast says dry, so it is ignored until it dries. It may need cleaning." The opt-in usage report counts it (`weather_note:sensor_stuck`): a name only, never which sensor.

title: PadSpan's own words match what it does; PadSpan's own words match what it does, round 3; Every website guide in German too; The help says what Alert pulse watches, and where a receiver's room is set; A leave alert's title says "left"; Guides and labels say what the panel says; The PadSpan HA Manual: start, the map, calibration, every day; The PadSpan HA Manual is complete: receivers, phones, tags, lights, the 3D house, running it; Sentences with a name in them, in German, French and Dutch; The everyday screens in German, French and Dutch; Settings' Appearance, Scanner Map and Tracking in German, French and Dutch; Setup's tools and Calibration in German, French and Dutch
body_markdown:
### New
- **Every website guide now has a German version.** The last three are in German now: connecting Claude to Home Assistant for Let Claude draw your rooms (padspan.traks.ca/guides/claude-ai-task/de/), the whole house on one wall in a large home (/guides/large-homes/de/) and which touch screen to hang for a PadSpan wall (/guides/wall-screens/de/). Each English page links its German one, and the guides list and the sitemap carry them.
- **What PadSpan is**, a new chapter of the manual in `docs/manual/` on GitHub: free and Pro, the editions, how it compares, and an "is it for me?" page that says plainly what Bluetooth can and can't do.
- **Requirements**: Home Assistant 2024.8 or newer, memory and Low-memory mode, and every kind of receiver, ESPresense and Tasmota included, with the one switch or command each needs.
- **Your first room in 15 minutes**: from install to Who's where now, a receiver's room picked right on the card, naming your phone, and on to a map.
- **Setup, step by step**: the plan, its scale, rooms, floor heights, receivers (with a room for one that has none), your phone or watch, Put it on the map and calibration; five ways to a plan when you have none; lining up floors.
- **Calibration**: when to calibrate and how many spots, Walk a room and how to turn it on, Guided calibration, Beacon Tune, reading Results and Accuracy by spot, and "Signals say this receiver is in …".
- **The screens**: Overview, Live Tracker, Follow, Occupancy, Traceback, Forensics, Health and the rest; Basic, Advanced and More tools; the sample house. Its menu map is made from the panel itself, and a test fails when the two disagree.
- **Alerts and notifications, all in one place**: Follow's movement alerts, the leak and smoke alarm banner, Alert pulse, Vacation Mode and guest notices, and Home Assistant's Repairs.
- **The manual in `docs/manual/` on GitHub has every chapter now**, from what PadSpan is to getting help, with the contents page linking each one.
- **Receivers, phones and tags**: which receivers to use and how many (ESPHome, Shelly, Home Assistant's own Bluetooth, ESPresense, Tasmota), where to put them, and PadSpan next to Bermuda; Android phones, iPhones and Apple Watches step by step; which tags work, AirTags, and lending a guest tag.
- **Rooms and floors come from Home Assistant**: how areas and floors become PadSpan's rooms, how floors are stacked, and the Rooms screen. **Walls and signal loss**: the materials, open edges, and steel doors that open with their sensor.
- **The Atlas** (with power teams: a wall dimmer and its smart bulbs as one light, Follow the day and a wake-up), **Live Aboard**, **Furnish** and **Wall screens and kiosks**, each in one chapter.
- **AI features**: connecting an AI Task or Claude, exactly what is read and where it goes, and what it costs.
- **Users and Enhanced security**, **Performance and small machines**, **Privacy: what leaves the house**, and **PadSpan Pro** (trial, keys, homes, testers, invites).
- **Appendices**: every screen and its tabs, the accuracy benchmark, and a part for developers with every websocket command. The screens table and the command table are made from the code, and a test fails when either no longer matches it.
- **More of the panel speaks German, French and Dutch.** When your Home Assistant profile is set to one of them, the menu and the phone's top bar, the messages that pop up, the update banner and What's new, the Overview, Who's where now, Follow (with Locate), Occupancy, Health with its list of problems, the status dot, the Receivers page, the IRK Manager, the Devices list and the device and receiver sheets now show their words in your language. The release notes themselves stay in English.
- **Problems and refusals in your language.** When PadSpan says no to something, or Health lists a problem, the sentence is shown in your language too. A sentence that names one of your rooms or devices is still in English for now.
- **Half of Settings speaks German, French and Dutch.** When your Home Assistant profile is set to one of them, the Settings tab strip and its tips, Appearance, Scanner Map and all of Tracking are in your language: room changes and timeouts, phones and guest tags (with the Phone Tracking setup guide), what the panel shows, positioning and calibration, receivers, performance, integrations (Automations, HA Tags, the Assist questions card, Ignore Bermuda) and privacy (Update Check, Enhanced security, the usage report).
- **Paths in the help and messages name the tabs as you see them.** "Settings → Tracking → Receivers" now reads in your language wherever the panel or its help says it.
- The Assist questions stay in English: Assist knows them only from the English sentences file, and the card says so.
- Settings' Features, AI, Atlas, UI Structure and licence tabs, Manage, Training, the Atlas and the 3D view are still in English; they come next.
- **Setup's tools and Calibration speak German, French and Dutch.** When your Home Assistant profile is set to one of them, Mapping (Upload, Edit with all its tools, 3D Stack with Floor Heights and Point Align, Layout), setting a plan's scale, the ways to a plan when you have none, the Setup Wizard's Put it on the map, the offers of Let Claude draw your rooms, and all of Calibration (guided calibration, Pin & Listen, Roam, Model, Results, Accuracy by spot, Walk a room, Tune and Beacon Tune) are in your language.
- **The rest of the device screens too.** Devices' By Room, Registry, Door Openers and relay wizard, the "same device?" lines and address badges, the Bluetooth page's Scanners, Advertisements, Visualisation and ESPHome configs tabs, and the overhead 2D map.
- Settings, Manage, Training, the Atlas and the 3D view are still in English; they come next.

### Changed
- **Health's problems that name a room, a plan or a receiver are in your language.** "Kitchen and Hall get mixed up", "Receiver “Hall proxy” often points to the wrong room", "Positions on “Ground” are often off" and the other System Critics that put a name or a number into their sentence used to stay in English in German, French and Dutch. The names stay as you gave them; numbers are written your language's way.
- **So are the most common refusals with a name in them**, such as "Kitchen is not a room on the map.", "There's no area called … in Home Assistant.", a file over the upload limit, a notification target that is gone, an IRK already saved for a phone, the usage report on a free licence, and the WLED team refusals.

### Fixed
- **The update notice names the right store.** It said "Update via HACS" on Marketplace installs too. It now says the Marketplace, HACS or, for a copy installed by hand, padspan_ha.zip from the release; when it can't tell, it names both stores. It finds out from Home Assistant itself, so it works without the internet.
- **"Room and receiver layout not built yet" says how to build it.** The Overview said the layout builds by itself from the drawn rooms. It doesn't: press Put it on the map on Setup's Finish step, or, in Advanced and Development modes, Commit this layout in Mapping → Layout.
- **A receiver's reliability is a figure to read, not a weight.** Health's help and the room-flapping guide said it is how much PadSpan trusts a receiver. Since 0.38.271 it is only shown: a low one doesn't make that receiver's readings count for less.
- **The Companion app path is Settings → Companion app → Manage sensors.** Training's troubleshooting, the Bluetooth page's Android tip and the Overview's "BLE transmitter is OFF" line left out the Companion app step.
- **Manage → HA Entities → Entity Type Library, the tracker card:** its state is the Home Assistant room name ("Kitchen"), it lists `padspan_id` and `last_room`, and it no longer says GPS trackers and PadSpan merge in a person: a phone's GPS or a router's "home" wins over a room.
- **Sub-zones are drawn with the Sub-zones tool in Mapping → Edit,** as Manage → HA Entities now says.
- **Installing by hand:** README and Getting started say to unzip `padspan_ha.zip` into `custom_components/padspan_ha`. The zip has no folder of its own.
- **The guest tags guide lists what the `padspan_ha_guest` event sends:** `session` too, `room` only for arrived, left and off_limits, and `how` for ended.
- **The bug report form** lists the receivers PadSpan reads (ESPHome Bluetooth proxy, Shelly, Home Assistant's own Bluetooth adapter, ESPresense, Tasmota), asks about Bermuda on its own, and shows current example versions.
- **Setup's steps in Setup's order, with the phone step.** Who's where now's help, Mapping's help and the Setup Wizard's help now list them as Setup does: plan, scale, rooms, floor heights, receivers, your phone or watch, calibration. So do the get-started guide and the README, which also say that Who's where now offers a room for each scanner with no area, with Set room.
- **The Setup Wizard saves each room as you finish it.** Its help still said to press Save Layout to keep the rooms.
- **Alert pulse flags any opening left open, not only doors.** Its text in Settings → Atlas now says what it does: a door, window, gate or cover left open for more than 6 hours, or a window or cover open while it rains or snows, rings its room in amber.
- **The iPhone steps point to the right place for the Keychain way:** Settings → Tracking → Phones and guest tags → Phone Tracking (Private BLE) → Detailed Setup Guide. They named a Settings tab that doesn't exist.
- **Follow's "No notify services found" names Home Assistant's real page,** Settings → Devices & services.
- **A doorway works for the scale.** The scale screen called a doorway "too short to trust", while the other screens suggest measuring one. PadSpan takes a doorway like any other length. The screen now says a doorway works, but a long wall is more exact.
- **The wall screen guide no longer tells portrait walls to choose Size for my room.** Since 0.38.181, Size from the screen draws a 4K wall at twice its 1080p size either way up, and the guide now says so, and that a TV which can't turn its picture can hang on its side with Screen orientation in Settings → Atlas → Wall screens. The large-homes guide said the same of landscape screens only.
- **Alert pulse, as the help describes it.** The help said it rings a room for "a door left open". It rings for any door, window, gate or cover left open over 6 hours, and a window or cover open while it rains or snows. Now in English, German, French and Dutch.
- **Who's where now's help names Set room.** It still said to give each receiver its area in Home Assistant; the card has had its own room picker since 0.38.276.
- **Follow's leave alert no longer says "departd".** The notification's title was built by adding a "d" to the event, which gave "PadSpan: Alex's phone arrived" for an arrival but "PadSpan: Alex's phone departd" for a leave. It now says "left", like the message under it.
- **Small wording fixes in the guides**, found while writing the manual: the guest tag guide names the lend dialog's field (Guest's name), the walls guide quotes the Enclose button as it reads, the wall screen guide quotes Protect against burn-in, and the phone tip spells the Companion app's menus as the app does.
- **The Overview's map is read out again.** The hidden text that tells a screen reader who is in which room stopped filling in after the last round of translations.
- **Mapping's receivers step says how to add a receiver.** It said to double-click the map, which made a marker Put it on the map does not use; it now says to press Add beside the receiver in Live BLE Receivers, then drag it into place.

title: Calmer bare floors in 3D; a tidier emergency button; The panel names Home Assistant's Areas, labels & zones menu; A bigger Atlas on a phone; room names you can read; The Atlas says what went wrong in plain words; The PadSpan HA Manual, first chapters; One next step for "no rooms yet"; Error messages in plain words; Problems in plain words; Each problem goes where it is fixed; Pick a receiver's room where PadSpan says it has none; Signals say this receiver is in another room; Setup: your phone or watch is a step; No leftover setup wording; Setup offers the quick room walk first; One place for "something's wrong"; Voice questions shown in the panel
body_markdown:
### New
- **One manual for PadSpan**, a chapter per page, in `docs/manual/` on GitHub. Its contents page lists every chapter planned and, for the ones still to come, the guide that covers that ground today. Home Assistant's "Documentation" link for PadSpan now opens it.
- **Install, update, uninstall.** Updating step by step, stable and betas, what PadSpan's own update notice says, and uninstalling step by step, with every file PadSpan leaves in Home Assistant's config folder and how to remove them. Floor plan pictures are in `padspan_ha/maps/` (not in `www/`, which anyone with the address could open).
- **Every entity, attribute, service and event PadSpan gives Home Assistant**, with the Assist intent, the MQTT topics and three automations to paste in. `last_room`, `room_reason`, `padspan_ha.set_room_tag_map` and `padspan_ha.wled_on` / `wled_off` were written down nowhere before.
- **Every setting**: where it is in the panel, its default, what it takes and what it does, including the ones on other screens and the ones the panel never shows.
- **Backups, restore, Factory Reset, and moving to a new Home Assistant machine.** Home Assistant's own backup carries all of PadSpan, and the chapter says which files. A Factory Reset also deletes PadSpan's own backups, so make a Home Assistant backup first.
- **Troubleshooting by symptom**, **getting help** (what each of the three reports holds and leaves out, and what to put in an issue) and a **glossary**.
- **The reference tables are made from the code**, and a test fails when they and the code disagree, so they describe the version they ship with.
- **A button on each problem that opens the screen that fixes it.** In Health's "Problems found", a floor plan with no scale has "Measure" (the scale step on that plan), rooms that get mixed up or old calibration have "Calibrate" (the guided calibration), rooms that don't fit their plan have "Open Layout" (Mapping → Layout on that floor), a receiver that often points to the wrong room has "Open Receivers", and learning switched off has "Open the setting" (in Basic, just that setting). A screen your mode doesn't have gets no button.
- **A receiver with no room gets its room picked right where PadSpan says so.** On the Overview's "Who's where now" and in Setup's receivers step, each receiver with no Home Assistant area now has a room list and "Set room". The room its name points to is already chosen ("esp32-kitchen" → Kitchen; change it if it's wrong). Set room gives the receiver that area in Home Assistant, exactly as the Bluetooth Radios list's Assign Area does, so the room shows everywhere at once. Like Assign Area, anyone in the house can use it; never on a wall screen.
- **Setup's receivers step suggests a receiver's room from what it hears.** Once you have calibration points, a receiver whose strongest-heard points are mostly in another room than the one it is filed under gets a line such as "Signals say Kitchen proxy is in Hall, not Kitchen: 3 of the 5 calibration points it hears best are there", with "Use Hall" (one tap sets that Home Assistant area for it) and "Keep Kitchen". It only speaks up when its own room has calibration points too, so a room you haven't calibrated yet never looks like the wrong one.
- **"Track your phone or watch" is now one of Setup's numbered steps**, after the receivers and before calibrating (which you walk with that phone). Its Start opens the phone setup wizard you already had (Bluetooth → IRK Manager → Track your phone); in Basic mode just that card, with the bar back to Setup over it. The step is done once PadSpan follows at least one phone or watch as yours: a phone or watch with its key (IRK) registered, or a Companion-app phone you pressed Track for. Getting started and the Setup Wizard's "Next" lines show the same step, numbered the same. An install that has the phone wizard switched off goes to the Overview's Track Your Phone card instead, opened.
- **The wizard's Android path ends with the one thing it was missing:** press Track for the phone on the Overview's Track Your Phone card, with a button that takes you there.
- **Setup's Calibrate step offers "Walk a room" first where it is switched on.** Its Start opens Calibration's Walk a room tab (walk each room for 90 seconds with your phone), and a "Point by point" button beside it opens Guided calibration as before. Where Walk a room is off (it still is by default), Start opens Guided calibration as it always did, and one line says how to turn the walk on, with "Open that setting" going straight to its switch (just that card in Basic mode).
- **Health says what the status dot says.** Clicking the dot opens Health, which now starts with the dot's own list (a receiver that went silent, positioning that stopped, learning paused), each line with a button to where you look into it: the Receivers page, Diagnostics or the Overview. Before, Health didn't mention most of them.
- **Diagnostics is one click from Health, and sends itself.** Health has "Open Diagnostics" (it was reachable only through QA). Diagnostics has "Email support" and "Open an issue" beside Copy: each copies the same report and opens an email to hello@traks.ca or a new GitHub issue to paste it into (issues are public, so remove personal details first).
- **"Which room is Alice in?" is explained where you set PadSpan up.** Home Assistant's Assist can answer which room someone is in, but only once its sentences are added to Home Assistant, and those were only in the online guide. Settings → Tracking → Home Assistant and integrations now has "Ask Assist which room someone is in": the questions as examples, in the name of one of your own devices, the answers it gives, and the sentences to save as `config/custom_sentences/en/padspan.yaml` with a "Copy the sentences" button.

### Changed
- **Live Aboard: bare rooms no longer look carpeted.** A room with nothing in it showed its colour and its motion glow as one flat, strong fill, so most rooms of a house not yet furnished read as navy, green or magenta carpets. A room's floor now takes its colour more softly the less furniture stands in it, and a bare room's motion glow is a lighter fill with the same bright edge. Each room keeps its own colour, lit lights and motion stand out more, and furnished rooms change only a little. In Classic, Studio and every Showcase look.
- **The Test emergency lighting button's corner.** The small list mark (tap the ring for every emergency light) now sits inside the ring instead of over its corner, and ☰ under the button has a clear gap and lines up with it, in Live Aboard and the flat Atlas.
- **The Atlas uses a phone's whole width.** On a phone the map sat in a narrow card beside a column of round buttons, so the house was a thumbnail. The buttons are now a row above the map and the map runs edge to edge. Desktops, tablets and wall screens look as they did.
- **The README's Troubleshooting link opens the troubleshooting chapter.**
- **With no rooms drawn, the Overview names one place to draw them.** Its 3D house said to draw rooms in Mapping → Layout, the room list said Mapping → Edit, and the "not built yet" banner said Mapping → Layout again, while Setup and Getting started say "Draw the rooms". All three now say Setup's Draw the rooms step, in every mode, and the room list and the banner have a "Draw the rooms" button that opens it.
- **When something can't be done, PadSpan says why in plain words.** About a hundred of the server's refusals named its internal parts: "ModelStore not loaded", "FabricStore not loaded", "Maps store not initialized", "barrier_id is required", "Entity '…' not found in registry". They are sentences now: "PadSpan hasn't finished loading. Try again in a minute; if this keeps happening, restart Home Assistant and look for PadSpan in its log.", "Pick a receiver first.", "Give the phone a name.", "There's no area called Kitchen in Home Assistant." Each keeps its error code, so nothing that reads them changes.
- **Error messages at the top of the panel show those sentences, not raw error text.** Some 175 places showed an error as it came, which could be "[object Object]", a bare "3" for a lost connection, Home Assistant's "required key not provided @ data['map_id']" or a page bug's "Cannot read properties of undefined". PadSpan's own message is shown as it is; for the rest you get a plain line that says what to do ("The connection to Home Assistant was lost. Wait a moment and try again.", "This page and the PadSpan on Home Assistant don't match. Refresh the page; if that doesn't help, restart Home Assistant.").
- **Health's "Problems found" now says what you would notice, in plain words.** Each check used to read like an engineer's log ("LOO mean error: 1.85 m", "Average RSSI variance 31.0 dBm²", "Scanner disagrees with consensus", "bidirectional transitions"). Now the title says what you'd see ("Kitchen and Hall get mixed up", "Receiver “Hall proxy” often points to the wrong room", "Signals in the Kitchen keep changing"), the message says why and the action what to do. The figures are all still there, on a "Details:" line under each card. The kinds and how serious each is are in words too ("Floor plan", "Receiver", "Signal and learning"; "Fix this", "Worth fixing", "Good to know"), and a floor is named the way Home Assistant names it, not by its id.
- **A new house is told its next step, not a critical problem.** With no calibration yet, Health said "No calibration data" as a critical problem, though rooms already come from the nearest receiver. It now says "Next step: calibrate". A floor plan uploaded but not measured yet is "Next step: set the scale" (still a warning once rooms or receivers are drawn on it), and when there are only next steps the banner says "NOTHING TO FIX". Every check is still there.
- **The status dot's "learning suspended" is said plainly:** "Learning is paused for now: rooms come from the live signals alone". The warning under Scanner Health says "1 receiver often points to a different room than the others" instead of "below 70% reliability".
- **Health → Scanner Health calls its last column "Reliability", what it is.** It said "Weight", but the figure is how often a receiver agrees with the room the others point to, from 0.5 to 1, and nothing is weighted by it. The help says so too, in every language.

### Fixed
- **The panel sends you to the menu Home Assistant actually has.** Nine places in the panel (Follow, Mapping, the Overview's receiver card, QA, Settings and Training) called Home Assistant's menu for rooms and floors "Areas & Zones"; on every Home Assistant PadSpan supports it is **Areas, labels & zones**.
- **Training's Quick Start names the Marketplace.** It only said to install through HACS and restart; on Home Assistant 2026.11 and newer you add PadSpan from Settings → Marketplace and its setup opens right away, with no restart. HACS, and the restart after it, is for older versions.
- **Room names on the Atlas stay readable.** A room's name could sit under a strip light, a person's badge or a tag's name ("Larder" under a strip, "Walk-in Closet" under a badge). The name now moves to a clear spot inside its own room, and back once someone walks off it. In a room too full for that, the name is drawn on top. The same on every floor and every Showcase theme.
- **The Atlas says what went wrong in plain words too.** When a scene, the emergency lighting, Vacation Mode, a preset, an intensity, a type override, a WLED switch or putting a light in a room failed, the Atlas showed the raw error ("[object Object]", Home Assistant's schema words). It now shows the same sentence the rest of PadSpan does: PadSpan's own reason as it is, and a plain line for a lost connection or a page that needs reloading.
- **Home Assistant's setup screens no longer carry wording for steps PadSpan doesn't have.** The integration's texts, in every language, still had a "Reconfigure PadSpan HA: Update scan interval" step, an options form and an "Update interval" field, all three gone from the setup long ago (how often PadSpan updates is set in the panel). They are removed, and a test now holds the texts to the steps the setup really shows.

title: Hiding device codes keeps names on the Atlas; The guides and the help say what PadSpan does today; The first screens in German, French and Dutch; Power teams on the map: one card for the wall dimmer and its bulbs, a wake-up, and the day's curve in the card; The usage report: power teams and colour bulbs
body_markdown:
### New
- **The first screens of the panel are in German, French and Dutch.** When your Home Assistant profile is set to one of them, the screens a new house meets first now speak it: the sample house's banner and the Data switch, Getting started, Setup with its steps, the Setup Wizard's own steps and buttons, Track Your Phone and the phone setup, and the Improve accuracy tips. Home Assistant's own menus are named as Home Assistant names them in your language. The rest of the panel is still English for now and will follow; any other language sees English as before.
- **A power team is one thing on the map.** Place the wall dimmer, one of its bulbs or the team's own light: a tap switches the team, a drag dims it, and a hold opens the team's card. A dimmer left on with its bulbs off shows dark, as the room is.
- **The team's card.** It says what the team is doing (off with the power on or cut, starting its bulbs, on but a bulb not answering, following the day, sleep, set by hand, waking up), with Follow the day and Sleep, the wall dimmer's power (on, left low at the wall, off or out of reach, with Cut power and Power on), and each bulb with its light, and Try again for one that did not answer. It updates while it is open.
- **Off can leave the power on.** Each team chooses what off does: turn the bulbs off and leave the power on, so they come back at once in the right colour, or cut the power as before. Teams you already have keep cutting the power; new teams leave it on. Change it in the card's Advanced section or in Settings → Atlas → Power teams.
- **A wake-up light.** On the days and at the time you choose, a team that is off comes on at its dimmest and warmest and fades to full light by then. Lights already on are left alone. Set it in the team's card.
- **The day's curve in the card,** with when this light's day starts and ends: the sun's sunrise and sunset moved by minutes, or fixed times (a bedroom whose day starts at 6:30 all year). Adapted from Adaptive Lighting, as the curve is.
- **Fades of any length.** A team's light now takes a transition, up to 100 minutes, so an automation can fade it in slowly; while it fades the day does not move it.
- **The opt-in usage report says how power teams are used, and which colour bulbs houses have.** A new line in the report, `power_teams`: how many power teams a house has, whether each has a wall control and what kind (a light or a switch, and which integration runs it, such as Control4, Lutron or Z-Wave), whether turning it off cuts the power or turns the bulbs off, whether it follows the day, has its own curve or a wake-up, and its bulbs by brand and integration. Team or not, it also counts the house's colour bulbs by brand (Hue, IKEA, Innr, LIDL, Ledvance, WiZ, Tuya and others) and by integration (a Hue Bridge, Zigbee2MQTT, ZHA and others), so the developer can see which bulbs people have. The power team card on the map also counts its buttons (opened, power cut or put back, Day, Sleep, Try again, a setting saved) and taps on the map that switch a team. Counts and words from a fixed list only, never a team's name, an entity, a time of day or a maker's own words. It is sent only with the report on, the Preview shows it, and the README's list of what the report sends has the new lines.

### Changed
- **The translated help names these screens as you see them.** Where the German, French or Dutch help mentions a button on the first screens, it now uses the translated word on the button; for the rest of the panel it still quotes the English name.

### Fixed
- **On the Atlas, hiding the device codes no longer hides the names of tags.** Names (a tag's, a guest's) stay on the map whatever the codes or the zoom; only the A01-style codes go.
- **Hidden device codes take the scanners' squares off the Atlas too.** With codes shown, scanners show as before.
- **The Atlas's tip and its key of shapes leave out what is hidden.** With the codes hidden the tip no longer says to tap a code, it names the read-only sensor tiles only while one is on the map, and the key of shapes lists only kinds the map draws.
- **The first-steps guides describe today's first run.** Getting Started still showed the February flow: a five-step wizard, a Sample mode switch, an Objects tab and dragging scanners on a map. It now follows what a new install does: it opens on your own house as soon as a scanner is heard, shows Who's where now, and Make it a map opens Setup, ending with Put it on the map. The website's first-steps guide (English and German) is brought up to 0.38.274, and the Floor Plan Setup page is rewritten: there is no master map, scanners are added from Live BLE Receivers, and nothing reaches the map of your house until Put it on the map.
- **The right tab everywhere.** The website, its guides in English and German, the wall screen guide and the last release notes still sent people to the Settings tab called Presence, which has been Tracking since 0.38.202. Each now names Tracking and the section the setting is in, such as Tracking → Rooms and timing → Home/Away Timeout for "Things keep their room". Wall screens are set in Settings → Atlas, the rooms editor is Mapping → Layout, the lights tool is Mapping → Atlas builder, and Floor Heights is on Mapping → 3D Stack.
- **The in-panel help had three wrong defaults, now right in English, German, French and Dutch:** Signal smoothing's Q is 3.0 with a range of 0.01 to 10 (it said 0.125, up to 1.0, from before November), the Bluetooth refresh interval is 5 seconds (it said 30), and Enhanced security is on for a new install (it said off). Home Assistant's menu is named "Areas, labels & zones", as it is.
- **An iPhone's key added in Home Assistant's Private BLE Device is picked up within five minutes**, not one; one added through PadSpan itself works straight away.
- **No more pointers to things that are gone or never were:** the HACS sign-in note (fixed upstream in October), three experimental features removed in August, home/away binary sensors (home or away is each device's tracker), Wi-Fi in occupancy, and the old WebSocket "API reference", now a short page on the entities, services and events to use instead. Troubleshooting links a page that helps, and Home Assistant 2024.8 is given as the minimum on the requirements page too.
- **The website's Pro list is complete** (placement on the Atlas, Live Aboard with Furnish, wall mode, the Atlas as Overview and its Heatmap, presets and Vacation Mode, Busy Times, Locate, Forensics and four themes), and its comparison with Bermuda and ESPresense is the README's, checked against their own docs.
- **A test keeps it that way:** it fails when a guide, the website, the help or a release note names a Settings tab, a part of a tab or a Mapping tab the panel doesn't have, or another Home Assistant minimum than the one HACS enforces.

title: The stable after 0.38.231: lights you tap in the 3D house, power teams, a phone's room scan as a floor plan, steadier rooms, and safer saves
body_markdown:
### New
- **This is everything since 0.38.231 in one go,** written as how it works now. The betas' notes under it are the steps along the way; where they differ, this one is right.
- **Lights in the 3D house.** Tap a light in Live Aboard to switch it. Lights show as buttons under where they hang, can be moved in the 3D editor, string lights are drawn, and a room can work as one light switch. Unlocking a lock from the map asks first, white-only bulbs get a warmth slider, and a light's card has a Details link to Home Assistant's own window for it.
- **Power teams.** Smart bulbs on a wall dimmer, or lights that always have power, act as one light that follows the day. Lights found on after a restart are put right.
- **No floor plan? Ways to get one.** Start a blank floor, use a drawing you have, or upload a phone's room scan: its rooms, doors, windows and furniture come with it, and it finds its own place. When a plan is moved, what was placed on it can move with it, and lining up plans can suggest a fit.
- **Let Claude draw your rooms (experimental).** With an AI Task set up, Claude reads a plan and proposes room outlines that you check and keep.
- **Live Aboard** opens on the whole house with labels that follow the zoom, glass walls, a look for each screen, room chips and a room panel, kitchen and bathroom furniture, one-tap room sets, people and cars, covered patios, open decks and an Outside floor, and a ready-made Christmas tree.
- **Keys can keep their room (an option, off unless you turn it on).** Settings → Tracking → Rooms and timing → Home/Away Timeout → Things keep their room: things no person carries can stay in their last room for hours. Every device's area sensor and tracker also gain `last_room`, the room it was last seen in.

### Changed
- **Home Assistant 2024.8 or newer.** It said 2024.1, but before 2024.8 the sensors of the devices PadSpan tracks could not be added. Every release from 2024.8 to 2026.11 is now tested on each change.
- **Rooms are steadier.** A device that goes quiet keeps its room instead of drifting to another, possibly on another floor; a device nobody heard no longer "arrives"; a pinned beacon reports its room once; and a room change is never sent twice running. On a real house's four-hour recording, wrong room changes for devices that never moved halved compared with 0.38.231, and repeated room-change events went from 882 to 3.
- **Room tracking never waits.** It stalled for half a minute or more each time a calibration point was added, while a model only the "Learned model" setting uses was retrained; that model now trains in the background, and only when that setting is on. The health pages and the device list next to a busy street are much faster.
- **Lighter Home Assistant database.** Signal readings and other per-poll values are no longer written to Home Assistant's history; rooms, home or away and names still are.
- **A new install starts with Enhanced security on.** A home already set up keeps the switch as it has it.
- **Receivers' agreement in System Critics now means what it says**, and it no longer changes room decisions.

### Fixed
- **Saves are checked.** A save of PadSpan's main files that does not reach the disk is reported in Settings → Repairs instead of passing silently, and the next good save takes the notice down.
- **A saved file PadSpan cannot read is kept,** renamed beside the others and named once in the log, instead of being written over.
- **Junk is refused in words:** a command with something missing, "nan" or "inf", numbers or texts too large to keep, and lists of the wrong kind. A settings save that is refused changes nothing at all.
- **Hidden devices stay hidden, and named devices stay listed** however long they are silent.
- **PadSpan does not fetch from your own machine:** a robot vacuum's or the ESPresense Companion's address must be a device on your network.
- **In the panel,** Escape closes every card and sheet, dialogs keep the keyboard and give it back, and wide tables on a phone scroll inside their own box.
